raw_case_text: A 46-year-old African American woman with HIV on ART (antiretroviral therapy) was admitted for progressively worsening dyspnea. She endorsed orthopnea, ankle swelling, and NYHA (New York Heart Association) class 3 symptoms for 2 weeks prior to admission. On examination, she was tachycardic, normotensive, and hypoxemic with distant heart sounds. She had a palpable left supraclavicular lymph node and multiple axillary lymph nodes. She also had tenderness in her right calf. Her white blood cell count was minimally elevated at 13 500 cells/mm3 with 78% neutrophils. D-Dimer was elevated at 20 microg/mL FEU (fibrinogen equivalent units; normal range: 0.00-0.48 microg/mL FEU). Chest radiograph showed cardiomegaly with no acute infiltrate. Electrocardiogram showed sinus tachycardia. An echocardiogram revealed moderate pericardial effusion with a normal ejection fraction. A diagnostic and therapeutic pericardiocentesis was performed due to concern for cardiac tamponade as she had an elevated troponin of 0.286 ng/mL (normal range: 0.0-0.034 ng/mL) and distant heart sounds. The pericardiocentesis drained serosanguinous fluid, which showed a normal white blood cells count with negative gram staining, thus ruling out infectious etiology. Venous Doppler of the right lower extremity revealed a deep vein thrombosis and she was started on heparin drip. A chest computed tomography (CT) angiogram showed no pulmonary embolism, but showed right paratracheal adenopathy, right hilar mass, and subcarinal nodes. CT abdomen/pelvis showed bilateral breast masses, bilateral pleural effusions, bilateral adrenal nodules, and vertebral translucency. Her brain magnetic resonance imaging showed 2 lesions, one in the cerebellum and one in the left frontal lobe consistent with metastasis. Her absolute CD4 count was 116 cells/microL (normal range: 500-1750 cells/microL), CD4 cells percentage was 7% (normal range: 30-61), and T-lymphocyte CD4/CD8 ratio of 0.11 (normal range: 0.86-5.00). She was started on prophylactic antibiotics with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole in addition to her antiretroviral treatment. An excision biopsy of the supraclavicular lymph node was consistent with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma with a mucin stain positive, immune staining using TTF-1 (thyroid transcription factor-1) positive and GATA-3 negative (ruling out metastatic breast adenocarcinoma). Pericardial fluid studies showed malignant large epithelioid cells, favoring metastatic adenocarcinoma. Over the course of her hospital stay, the patient continued to have worsening dyspnea, prompting further drainage of her re-accumulating pericardial fluid with a pericardial window. However, after the procedure was performed, the patient expired as a result of her decompensating status.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 46-year-old female presenting with progressively worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, and bilateral ankle swelling for two weeks.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 46-year-old female presented with a 2-week history of progressively worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, lower extremity edema, and NYHA functional class 3 symptoms, prompting acute hospital admission.
subjective.past_medical_history: Underlying immunodeficiency on established antiretroviral therapy (ART); no other prior medical comorbidities documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Orthopnea, ankle swelling, NYHA class 3 dyspnea, right calf pain/tenderness; denies chest pain or fever.

objective.physical_examination: Admission vitals: Tachycardic, normotensive, hypoxemic. Cardiovascular: Distant heart sounds. Lymphatics: Palpable left supraclavicular lymphadenopathy and multiple palpable axillary lymph nodes. Extremities: Right calf tenderness and ankle swelling.
objective.routine_investigations: White blood cell count: 13,500 cells/mm3 with 78% neutrophils. D-dimer: 20 microg/mL FEU (normal: 0.00-0.48 microg/mL FEU). Cardiac troponin: 0.286 ng/mL (normal: 0.0-0.034 ng/mL). Chest radiograph: Cardiomegaly without acute pulmonary infiltrates. Electrocardiogram: Sinus tachycardia. Echocardiogram: Moderate pericardial effusion with normal left ventricular ejection fraction. Pericardiocentesis fluid: Serosanguinous fluid with normal WBC count and negative Gram stain. Venous duplex ultrasound of right lower extremity: Deep vein thrombosis.
objective.advanced_workup: Chest CT angiogram: Negative for pulmonary embolism; demonstrated right paratracheal lymphadenopathy, right hilar mass, and subcarinal lymph nodes. CT abdomen/pelvis: Bilateral breast masses, bilateral pleural effusions, bilateral adrenal nodules, and vertebral translucency. Brain MRI: Two lesions located in the cerebellum and left frontal lobe consistent with metastases. Excision biopsy of left supraclavicular lymph node: Metastatic adenocarcinoma of lung origin, mucin stain positive, thyroid transcription factor-1 (TTF-1) positive, GATA-3 negative. Pericardial fluid cytology: Malignant large epithelioid cells favoring metastatic adenocarcinoma.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Metastatic lung adenocarcinoma (Stage IV with metastases to lymph nodes, pericardium, brain, adrenals, and vertebrae) complicated by malignant pericardial effusion, impending cardiac tamponade, and right lower extremity deep vein thrombosis, in a patient with advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV; absolute CD4 count 116 cells/microL [normal 500-1750], CD4 percentage 7% [normal 30-61%], CD4/CD8 ratio 0.11 [normal 0.86-5.00]).
Management & Outcome: Managed with unfractionated heparin infusion for DVT, prophylactic trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, continued ART, and therapeutic pericardiocentesis. Due to rapid pericardial re-accumulation and refractory respiratory failure, a surgical pericardial window was performed; however, the patient experienced acute clinical decompensation and expired shortly after surgery.
